headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while n8n can write and exfiltrate workflow data by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, and supported app content, while n8n workflows can process arbitrary upstream content and pass it into AI Agent nodes. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if n8n forwards untrusted text into ChatGPT prompts. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier in the profiles, so uncertainty does not justify lowering severity.
conditions: IF n8n forwards untrusted workflow text into a ChatGPT prompt without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to follow instructions embedded in files or screenshots, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Sanitize and strip instructions from any n8n-fed text before prompting ChatGPT.
Add a fixed system prompt that ignores instructions from workflow inputs.
Use a human review step before executing any AI-generated action.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and prompt-boundary enforcement between n8n and ChatGPT.
Restrict ChatGPT to read-only summarization for n8n-supplied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while n8n can read and write server files and send data through broad integrations. In default workflows, sensitive content can move from ChatGPT into n8n and then out to third-party services without a strong built-in isolation boundary. The blast radius includes secrets and work products, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop is given sensitive files or screenshots and n8n receives the resulting text, leakage can propagate to connected systems.
IF an n8n workflow uses external integration nodes on data derived from ChatGPT outputs, data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Limit n8n workflows to non-sensitive test data.
Disable or remove external integration nodes for the workflow.
Redact secrets before passing ChatGPT output into n8n.
Use separate credentials and accounts for the two agents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks at the workflow boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read access to user files and clipboard/screen surfaces, while n8n has server filesystem write and shell execution. If both are pointed at the same workspace or connected systems, they can race on shared mutable state even though ChatGPT itself cannot write files. The conflict is real but narrower than unrestricted dual-write, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or connected system, n8n writes can overwrite artifacts ChatGPT is reading.
IF n8n Execute Command is used on files ChatGPT is inspecting, concurrent edits can corrupt state.
mitigations: Separate read-only and write-only directories.
Pause n8n writes while ChatGPT is inspecting shared artifacts.
Use file locking in the workflow.
Keep ChatGPT on copies, not live files.
requires-engineering: add orchestration-level locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestration layer that can execute downstream actions, and ChatGPT Desktop can generate text from files, screenshots, and app context. If n8n treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, a mistaken summary can trigger emails, API calls, or file writes. Because the pair is designed for tool chaining, the default blast radius can extend beyond one work product.
conditions: IF n8n uses ChatGPT output as a direct trigger for workflow actions, errors can cascade into external side effects.
IF ChatGPT summarizes source material without verification and n8n executes the summary, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require a verification step before any n8n action.
Use schema validation on ChatGPT outputs.
Constrain ChatGPT to produce citations or structured fields only.
Add a manual approval gate for destructive workflow steps.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based routing and rollback for workflow actions.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. If regulated data enters ChatGPT and then flows into n8n-connected systems, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, but the mismatch risk is material.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by both agents, their logging and retention settings must be aligned.
IF n8n routes ChatGPT-derived data to external integrations, residency and DPA requirements may change.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Review retention settings for both systems.
Store secrets only in n8n credential vaults.
Document the data flow for each workflow.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
